subject: Request: current SOC 2 Type II and auditor-signed bridge for procurement
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@alphahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for current SOC 2 Type II and auditor-signed bridge for procurement

Hi Jasmine,

We're in the middle of a procurement review for a data processing agreement and the security team flagged that the SOC 2 Type II report we downloaded from your portal lists an audit period ending 2023-09 and is marked as the current public report. Our procurement deadline is May 27 and they require either: (1) the most recent auditor-signed SOC 2 Type II covering a later audit period, or (2) an auditor-signed bridge/attestation that extends coverage until a reissued report is available.

Can you confirm whether a reissued Type II is available or if your auditors will provide a signed bridge letter? If neither is available, can you share interim evidence (system description, SIG/CAIQ, compensating controls) and an ETA for reissue?

Thanks—this is blocking the legal sign-off.

Emma Stone
Senior Procurement Manager
Alpha Health Tech
emma.stone@alphahealth.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@alphahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for current SOC 2 Type II and auditor-signed bridge for procurement

Hi Emma—thanks for the note and the timeline. I've looped in Neha from our security & compliance team and Dylan from SE so we can give an accurate auditor-status update and share any interim artifacts that meet your procurement requirements.

Quick answers up front:
- I see the public SOC 2 we published covers Oct 2022–Sep 2023.
- I do not have a reissued PDF in my mailbox today.

Neha — can you confirm auditor reissue status and whether an auditor-signed bridge is possible before May 27? If not, we can surface a SIG (or CAIQ) and a short addendum for procurement to accept as temporary mitigation.

Emma — if you have a preferred format (signed bridge vs. contract addendum vs. SIG), let me know and we'll prioritize. Happy to set a 15-min call if that helps move this along.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma.stone@alphahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for current SOC 2 Type II and auditor-signed bridge for procurement

Hi all—quick compliance update.

Background: Our last publicly posted SOC 2 Type II covers the period 2022-10 through 2023-09. We completed the follow-up audit fieldwork in March 2026; the auditor (Hillside & Co.) is finalizing their report and supporting documentation. Redaction/review with legal is underway.

Current position: As of today there is no auditor-signed "reissued" Type II PDF we can publish. An auditor-signed bridge/letter is a statement from the auditor attesting to controls in effect during the gap period and must be prepared and signed by Hillside & Co. We have requested that they issue either (a) a bridge letter or (b) the finalized Type II report by 2026-05-25. That said, we do not control their internal timelines and cannot guarantee the exact sign date.

Interim materials we can provide immediately:
- System Description and controls mapping (internal)
- Completed SIG questionnaire export (I attached a tailored SIG excerpt for your review)
- A short "Audit Status Note" explaining the auditor engagement status and expected ETA (attached)
- A proposed procurement addendum (no legal signatures) that codifies short-term compensating controls and references the pending report (attached).

If Alpha Health requires an auditor-signed bridge specifically for legal sign-off, we will press Hillside for formal confirmation and will share any auditor communication as soon as we get it. In parallel, the SIG + addendum usually suffices for procurement teams as temporary mitigation.

Attachments: SOC2_Public_2023-09.pdf (public copy), Audit_Status_Note_20260518.txt, SIG_Questionnaire_AHT.xlsx, Proposed_Procurement_Addendum.docx

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@alphahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for current SOC 2 Type II and auditor-signed bridge for procurement

Thanks Neha—appreciate the clarity. Two follow-ups from procurement: (1) they explicitly require an auditor-signed bridge or a reissued Type II to complete their checklist; a vendor-generated addendum alone won't satisfy legal in this case, and (2) they're asking for auditor communication (email or note) confirming the expected sign date.

Can Redwood get Hillside & Co. to provide a short confirmation (even an email) that they're targeting May 25 for reissue or will provide a bridge by May 27? That confirmation is usually enough to unblock legal pending receipt of the signed artifact. If that's not feasible, procurement will escalate to security leadership but may have to put our contract on hold.

Appreciate any expedited help here—deadline is May 27.

Emma
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@alphahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for current SOC 2 Type II and auditor-signed bridge for procurement

Emma—thanks, understood. Next steps from our side:

1) Neha will continue to push Hillside for a one-line confirmation (email) with their targeted sign date. I'll follow up with the auditor contact this afternoon to escalate.

2) In parallel, I'm attaching the interim artifacts (SIG spreadsheet excerpt + Audit Status Note) and a proposed procurement addendum that Alpha Health's legal can sign. If procurement will accept the auditor confirmation email (even if the signed PDF follows shortly after), that should be sufficient for most PO workflows.

3) If Alpha Health requires an explicit 3rd-party-signed document immediately, we can offer a short-term commercial concession (e.g., a 30-day security hold-back or credit) while the auditor completes their signed issuance. Happy to surface options in a 10–15 minute call.

Link to interim artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleLink

Can we set a 10-min call tomorrow morning PT to confirm the acceptability of the addendum vs. waiting for the auditor email? Proposed times: Wed 05/20 09:00 or 09:30 PT.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
